correctness.rationale: PASS: all 35,367 nonempty simplices arise by exhaustive endpoint-disjoint edge selection on the explicitly labeled LCF Pappus graph. A stagewise vertex-toggle matching with 17,660 pairs leaves critical counts 1 in dimension 0, 43 in dimension 5, and 3 in dimension 6. Full topological sort of 191,349 oriented covering incidences proves acyclicity. Exact signed gradient-path recursion gives a 43x3 integral boundary with rows 30,13,27 equal to -I3, so the image is primitive of rank 3. In the simply connected CW model with only zero-, five- and six-cells, pi_5 of the wedge of forty-three S5 copies is Z43; unimodular attaching degrees cancel exactly three S5 summands. This proves wedge^40 S5, with no torsion; independent exact F2 chain elimination reproduces rank 40. A verifier source file and cross-check source file are embedded.

originality.rationale: PASS with specific residual bibliographic risk: full prior same-object RESULT.md yields only F2 homology and expressly excludes integral and homotopy determinations; the new integral primitive Morse differential strictly strengthens it. Original full texts of Donovan–Scoville, Kozlov, manifold matching-complex and honeycomb perfect-matching-complex papers were read; their statements have different objects or restricted hypotheses, so no implication covers Pappus. Aliases, stronger graph families and exact tables were searched in published-finding corpus and public literature; this is evidence of a gap, not proof of global uniqueness.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently titled integral Pappus matching-complex computation could exist; indexed search cannot prove global novelty.
The published mod-two result has exact face counts, so new contribution depends crucially on the independently verified primitive integral differential and wedge cancellation.
The honeycomb graph alias does not make the ordinary complex equivalent to any perfect-matching complex; the distinction is face-definition-specific.
